title: Analysis visualization overwrites same-named user materials
source: Untrusted .blend material datablocks whose names collide with PJ_Overlay_0..5, PJ_Gap, or PJ_Blend.
control: The new helpers use bpy.data.materials.get(name) but do not require an add-on ownership tag or leave an existing unowned material unchanged.
sink: Assignments to use_nodes, diffuse_color, and roughness mutate the selected global material datablock.
impact: Invoking Calculate Coverage with visualization can silently alter user-owned material data, including material users in other objects or scenes, and the changes persist if the file is saved.
proof: get_overlay_material reuses an existing fixed-name material at line 119 and writes it at lines 123-124; gap and blend builders do the same at lines 481-483 and 511-513. The Blender smoke test protects only a same-named collection, not material collisions.
closest_apparent_control: Blender auto-renaming is effective only when materials.new is called; the existing-name branches bypass it and no pj_owner check exists.
plausibility: The full source-to-sink path is in the changed code and requires only a same-named material plus the normal Analyze action.

validation.method: static code trace against Blender datablock lookup semantics and repository collision test
validation.evidence: All three branches directly reuse and mutate bpy.data.materials.get results; no intervening ownership or creation-only check exists.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Analyze is an explicit UNDO-capable local operator, and each collision uses a reserved-looking name; neither prevents persisted modification after save.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: No headful Blender reproduction was run in this worker.

attack_path.dataflow: crafted or user-owned same-named material -> bpy.data.materials.get -> visualization property assignments
attack_path.reachability: Open the .blend and invoke Calculate Coverage with Build Visualisation enabled (default).
attack_path.counterevidence: No automatic execution on file load; Blender Undo may recover before saving.
attack_path.severity_rationale: The path crosses the untrusted-scene boundary and corrupts user-owned scene datablocks, but requires an explicit local operator action and affects bounded material fields.
attack_path.change_conditions: Use uniquely created owner-tagged materials or refuse to mutate existing unowned materials.

title: Unbounded arc-length tessellation can exhaust Blender resources
source: A typed or loaded finite pj_wall.radius combined with a valid arc and a coverage gap or blend span.
control: The RNA radius property has soft_max=100 but no hard max, and CylindricalWall requires only finite positive radius and at-most-full-circle sweep.
sink: _band_geometry computes steps=ceil(width/0.25) and allocates/appends two vertices per step plus one face per step without a maximum.
impact: A malformed or adversarial .blend can make the normal Analyze action freeze Blender or exhaust memory while creating gap/blend overlay meshes.
proof: A valid radius of 100000 m and full-circle arc produces 628318.53 m arc length, 2513275 loop steps, 5026552 vertices, and 2513275 faces for one full-width band. The calculation was reproduced with the current CylindricalWall class; visualization has no cap before mesh construction.
closest_apparent_control: samples, grid_s, grid_z, and wall mesh segments are hard-bounded, but physical band subdivision is independent of those bounds; soft_max affects UI sliders only.
plausibility: A projector at the cylinder center can hit a portion of a 100000 m-radius wall within compute_footprint's 1000000 m ray limit, leaving a large gap that reaches the sink.

validation.method: static source-to-sink trace plus bounded pure-core arithmetic reproduction
validation.evidence: Current core accepted radius=100000 and a full-circle wall, yielding 2,513,275 band steps at the hard-coded 0.25 m subdivision; changed visualization loops and allocates proportionally.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: The user must invoke Analyze with visualization enabled and a non-empty gap/blend interval; no background execution occurs on load.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: The worker intentionally did not attempt the multi-million-face allocation in Blender because it risks workstation denial of service.

attack_path.dataflow: untrusted wall radius/arc in .blend -> CylindricalWall arc_length -> coverage interval width -> _band_geometry step count -> Python lists and Blender mesh allocation
attack_path.reachability: Open the crafted scene, retain a partially hitting projector, and invoke Calculate Coverage with default visualization.
attack_path.counterevidence: Numeric values must be finite and sweep is limited to one revolution; neither bounds radius or derived arc length.
attack_path.severity_rationale: The threat model explicitly treats reliable crafted-scene unbounded resource use as medium; the action can hang or OOM Blender but does not execute code or access files/network.
attack_path.change_conditions: Cap derived tessellation steps or subdivide against a configured hard maximum independent of physical dimensions.

title: Plan Array replacement deletes projectors without the add-on ownership check
source: Untrusted .blend collection membership plus pj_projector.is_projector and pj_generated custom-property state on an object.
control: Replacement checks only is_projector and pj_generated; unlike every newly generated array object and clear_collection, it does not require obj[pj_owner] == projection_planner.
sink: bpy.data.objects.remove(..., do_unlink=True) deletes the object and bpy.data.cameras.remove deletes its orphaned camera datablock.
impact: Opening a crafted or malformed scene and invoking the default Plan Projector Array action can delete user-owned objects placed in the adopted PJ Projectors collection; multiple objects can be removed before replacement.
proof: replace_existing defaults true at lines 357-360. The deletion predicate at line 400 omits OWNER_KEY, while created objects receive OWNER_KEY at line 410 and clear_collection explicitly checks it at visualization.py:100.
closest_apparent_control: Dedicated collection lookup and generated/projector markers narrow the set, but all are persisted scene state and the code's designated object-level ownership marker is not checked.
plausibility: The operation is reachable from the standard panel and the deletion executes before creating replacements; no validation distinguishes user-owned from add-on-owned objects.

validation.method: static code trace and comparison with the adjacent ownership-control pattern
validation.evidence: The default operator iterates the add-on collection and directly removes every object satisfying two scene-controlled markers; OWNER_KEY is demonstrably available and used for creation and analysis cleanup but absent from this predicate.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: The operation is explicit and UNDO-capable, and the object must be in the tagged projector collection; a crafted .blend can satisfy those persisted preconditions.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: No destructive Blender reproduction was run because static reachability is direct and exercising it would mutate a scene.

attack_path.dataflow: crafted .blend object membership/properties -> replace_existing predicate -> Blender object/camera removal
attack_path.reachability: Open the scene and click Plan Projector Array; Replace Existing is enabled by default.
attack_path.counterevidence: The sink is limited to one tagged collection and Blender Undo may recover the action before save; there is no automatic load-time deletion.
attack_path.severity_rationale: The path can delete user-owned scene objects across the untrusted .blend boundary, but needs explicit local action and crafted persisted markers; the scope is narrower than arbitrary filesystem deletion.
attack_path.change_conditions: Require the same OWNER_KEY/OWNER_ID check used by clear_collection, and avoid adopting unowned objects based solely on generated/projector flags.
